label: D1 after an a2 -> S2 common transition (stronger when unrewarded)
explanation: Fires only at D1 (none at GO or D2). It needs the previous trial to be a2 that reached S2 by a common transition: 80% of activation mass falls here, and it almost never fires after a1 or after a rare transition (0.4% of mass). Most of the remaining misses are rel -3 D1 steps, where the previous trial lies outside the window and cannot be checked. Precision is only 0.34. The feature is silent on many a2->S2c trials, especially during long stable runs of rewarded a2->S2c, where activation decays over successive repeats. It is stronger when the previous trial was unrewarded (adding prev_reward == 0 gives precision 0.62 and covers 64% of the top activation quartile), and also stronger early in the episode or right after a reversal. Adding a recent-history condition (unrewarded, or a2 not chosen two trials back) raised F1 only to 0.50, so I recorded the simpler predicate. Uses only observed variables.
